summary: WebGL 2.0 is a Khronos Group specification that lets a web page draw three-dimensional graphics into an HTML canvas element through an interface that follows OpenGL ES 3.0. It covers the drawing calls themselves, shader programs in the OpenGL ES Shading Language, instanced drawing, a named opt-in extension mechanism and an official conformance test suite. It leaves everything above the drawing call to others, including scene description, materials, lighting, cameras, file formats, sound, input, networking and identity. Traps for a standards audience: the text describes only the differences from WebGL 1.0, so both documents must be read together; it is not entirely backwards compatible with WebGL 1; compressed texture formats come only from optional extensions; and the separate compute-shader draft is marked obsolete, with WebGPU named as the path forward.
